title: Use Matlab code (rather than Autolev/C) for the accelerometer model in SimuAccGyro.m
body:
We already do this in the 3D model, and it would make the code much easier to understand and more consistent between models.

The calculations will start with the forward kinematics function that already exists, and will always exist in future versions.

This will also make it easier to transition to a version where we no longer use Autolev (like Gait2d in FEModel branch in BioSimToolbox).

There is one drawback, the 3D IMU code does finite difference for the accelerometer jacobian, but it only requires nDof function evaluations. And in the 2D model we may be able to do that analytically too.

After confirming that results are still the same, all the accelerometer related Autolev and C code will be removed, and corresponding build script code in Matlab.

@adkoele Before starting on this, I would like to hear if this is a good idea.
author: tvdbogert

comments.body: I think that it makes sense to do this, as long as the results are indeed still the same. I was just wondering about the 3D code though, because the finite difference method seems to be doing only 1 function evaluation and not nDof as you describe here. It is in lines 86-92 in simuAccGyro.

You are right! Another good reason to do this, it would be very efficient.

In the 2d model, we had the model coefficients a and their dependence on q,qd,qdd was "hidden" in the Autolev code.  So we had to do finite differences on each degree of freedom to construct the Jacobians da/dq, da/dqd, da/dqdd (when the Jacobian code in C crashed, which does not happen anymore).

In the 3d model, we calculate the accelerometer signals from the forward kinematics FK,  and 1st and second time derivatives FKd, FKdd.

The Autolev/C code for FK generates 3 outputs: FK, and the Jacobians dFK/dq and dFKd/dq.

From this we generate FKd = dFK/dq * qd  and FKdd = d/dt (FKd) = dFKd/dq * qd

And the Jacobians dFKd/dqd = dFK/dq, dFKdd/dqd = dFKd/dq

The only one that requires finite difference is dFKdd/dq, and we use

dFKdd/dq = d/dt (dFKd/dq) = (dFKd/dq (t+h) - dFKd/dq (t) ) /h 

The input to the FK function is not t, but q and qd, so we use

        q(t+h) = q + h*qd;
        qd(t+h) = qd + h*qdd;

I think Eva came up with this, or maybe it was me.

It may even be possible to write the IMU code in a more general way, so it works for both the 2d and 3d models.  They will have a lot on common. Then we would put it in the Model superclass?  @adkoele please confirm.

This is not a high priority, but I will work on it in the coming month.

Yes, I was thinking the same, that it could be a common code that is used by both/all models. However, I am not that familiar with this code, so I might miss something. P.S. I might have accidentally removed a branch when cleaning up my local copy of the code.

I am familiar enough with both the 2D and 3D IMU code.  They will be essentially the same except for the FK being a 3D position and 3x3 matrix in 3D, as opposed to 2D position and 2x2 matrix in 2D.  It could be something like:

```
if isa(obj, 'Gait2dc')
   % convert 2d FK outputs to 3d equivalent
end
% now calculate the IMU outputs
```

Longer term, it would not be a terrible idea to do all modeling in 3D, and a 2D model would have no movement in the 3rd dimension.  That is how OpenSim does it.  The FK function would return 3D position and orientation even for a 2D model.  Then a lot of code would be in the superclass Model.  Muscles could also be coded to be compatible with both 2d and 3d.
About the branch, yes, I noticed some of my changes were gone, it was easy to redo.  Glad it was something you noticed and not a mysterious failure.
